interactions.summary: A student treats Dante's use of Paul as inconsistent with his criticism of the Church, and Jiang narrows that objection: Dante wants reform, not abolition, but the deeper oddity remains.
Another student points out that Dante seems to fall back into rote theological recitation after praising imagination and inward inquiry, and Jiang agrees the situation is genuinely strange.

After rereading Hebrews, Jiang argues that the paradox is structural: if Paul is the expert on faith, Paul's absence from the heavenly examination signals that Dante is repeating official doctrine only to alter it.

speaker_notes.note: The student's phrasing conflates Paul with the Catholic Church, but the usable pressure is the tension between Dante's institutional criticism and his appeal to apostolic authority.

claims.claim: Jiang says it is too strong to say Dante despises the Catholic Church; his position is that the Church should be reformed rather than abolished.
A student argues that Dante appears inconsistent because he praises imagination and inward searching but answers Peter's question by reciting authoritative doctrine.
Jiang agrees that the scene is paradoxical and uses Hebrews 11 to show that Dante is staging an encounter with official doctrine rather than simply rejecting it.
Jiang argues that if Paul is the true expert on faith, his absence from the heavenly examination matters: Dante is signaling distance from official teaching even while quoting it.
Jiang predicts that Dante will keep the official definition of faith on the surface while introducing subtle revisions to its meaning.

signature_moments.moment: The class catches Dante in apparent self-contradiction: after attacking rote theology, he suddenly answers with rote theology.
signature_moments.source_phrase: he's reciting something and he's spilling it out
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It sharpens the interpretive problem Jiang is trying to solve in the faith canto.

signature_moments.moment: Paul's absence becomes evidence in itself: if Dante were simply orthodox, Paul would be the examiner.
signature_moments.source_phrase: otherwise why not have paul test you
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's cleanest statement of how Dante marks a difference from official teaching without openly breaking from it.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's label for the Pauline definition of faith that Dante cites before, in Jiang's view, modifying it.
Jiang's boundary on Dante's anti-Church posture: institutional criticism aimed at repair rather than destruction.

chronology_notes.note: On 2026-06-17 Jiang interprets Dante's treatment of faith as a reformist maneuver inside orthodoxy: he cites official doctrine while signaling that it is insufficient in its current form.

uncertainty_notes.note: The long Hebrews reading is present mainly as source setup. The packet keeps its stable function in Jiang's argument rather than extracting every Biblical proposition as a new claim.
